officialSources.name: Halmstad municipality: Vandringsleder och motionsspår
facts: Municipality describes Prins Bertils stig as beginning at Halmstad slott and ending at Möllegård.
Municipality lists Prins Bertils stig length as 18 km.
Municipality says the trail has outdoor gym, playground, grill places with benches, several bathing places, Rhododendronparken and toilets at several places.

officialSources.name: Destination Halmstad: Prins Bertils stig
facts: Destination Halmstad describes Prins Bertils stig as an 18 km coastal walking trail from central Halmstad to Tylösand and onward to Möllegård.
The page divides the trail into Halmstad slott - Västra stranden, Västra stranden - Grötvik, Grötvik - Tylösand and Tylösand - Möllegård.
This source is useful for corridor context but is not exact K7 geometry because K7 ends at Halmstad C and does not continue to Möllegård.

officialSources.name: Halmstad municipality: Stränder och badplatser
facts: Municipality says beach toilets are open and rubbish is collected from June to September.
Tylösand is a major official beach and part of a four-kilometre beach stretch.
Tjuvahålan is a small family beach with rocks and jetty; Prins Bertils stig passes it and the municipality lists fishing, grill place and toilet there.
Svärjarehålan is one of two accessible sea baths, staffed 16 June to 17 August, 09.00-17.00, but staff are not lifeguards.
Tylösand, Frösakull, Ringenäs and Villshärad are summer-monitored by trained lifeguards; red flag means dangerous bathing.

officialSources.name: Halmstad municipality: Hundar och hästar på stranden
facts: Dogs are prohibited on municipal official bathing beaches between 1 May and 15 September.
Horses are prohibited on official bathing beaches between 1 May and 15 September.
Riding in sea-shore dunes is never allowed.
Dogs are welcome year-round on non-official beaches if under close control.

officialSources.name: Länsstyrelsen Halland: Alet nature reserve
facts: Alet/Aleskogen is a Halmstad nature reserve of about 54 hectares, protected since 2019, owned and managed by Halmstad municipality.
The route overlay indicates K7 crosses Alets naturreservat around km 10.746-11.972.
Visitor information says Prins Bertils stig has an accessible dry toilet in the area and the reserve has two arranged grill places.
Rules include no fires except at designated places, dogs leashed with max 2 m leash, no motor vehicles/parking except designated places and no tenting without municipal permission.

officialSources.name: Halmstad municipality: Brandriskprognos and Eldningsförbud
facts: As accessed on 2026-04-30, Halmstad said no fire-risk assessment was currently being made and assessment normally runs May-September.
Halmstad fire-ban page explains that fire bans apply in forest and land outside built-up areas and that some municipal grill places may still be safe places depending on ban level.
Fire-ban status is dynamic and must be rechecked immediately before import/publication.

officialSources.name: Hallandstrafiken and ResRobot planning sources

officialSources.name: OpenStreetMap / Overpass corridor checks

routeCharacter: Coastal and urban section following much of the Prins Bertils stig corridor in the reverse direction from Tylösand toward central Halmstad.
Starts at Tylösand beach and Tyludden with views toward Tylön and the Tylöbukten coast.
Passes Tjuvahålan and Svärjarehålan, including an accessible sea-bathing area.
Continues through Grötvik with harbor, old quarry and rocky coastal context.
Passes Brottet and crosses Alet/Aleskogen nature-reserve terrain before approaching Västra stranden.
Follows urban/coastal paths along Nissan, Halmstad slott and Slottsbron to Halmstad C/Resecentrum.
geometryImportDecision: Use official GPX/API geo_json as canonical K7 geometry.
Preserve the single continuous LineString and exact endpoints.
Suppress API line.geometry because it is missing/unusable.
Do not import Prins Bertils stig, OSM inland Hallandsleden relation or nearby bicycle routes as K7 geometry.
Record 15 km official display distance while preserving 14.7 km GPX description, 14.673 km computed length and 14.6 km Naturkartan contradiction.

Dogs are allowed on non-official beaches under close control.
Alet requires dogs leashed with max two-meter leash except marked exception area.
Naturvårdsverket general rule requires extra control of dogs in nature 1 March-20 August.
horseRules: Horses/riding are prohibited on official bathing beaches between 1 May and 15 September.
Riding in sea-shore dunes is never allowed.
Nearby reserves may further restrict riding, but Alet-specific horse rule was not identified in the checked visitor rule summary.
campingRules: Alet prohibits tenting without municipal permission.
Halmstad local public-place rules allow camping or equivalent overnighting in vehicles only at places/areas and times designated by the municipality.
No official free K7 campsite or trail shelter was found.
fireRules: Alet allows fires only at designated places.
Halmstad fire-risk page said no brandriskbedömning was active as accessed 2026-04-30; the normal assessment season is May-September.
During fire bans, municipal and rescue-authority rules control whether any grill place can be used.
Fire status must be rechecked immediately before import/publication.
seasonalAndCurrentness: Beach toilets/rubbish are seasonal in municipal beach operations, but the K7 official places feed marks most corridor toilets as year-round.
Tylösand and Svärjarehålan have summer beach staffing/lifeguard or beach-host context, with red-flag water-safety caveats.
Halmstad C railway/station works and Halmstad Stationsstaden planning continue through 2026-2029; import as end-point currentness watch, not closure.
Halmstad municipality reports Grötvik future planning/work beginning in 2026 with possible adoption by Q2 2029; import as future works watch only.
Halmstad municipality reported a 2025 Prins Bertils stig strandskydd/dispens issue at Sandhamn but said the trail should remain; import as legal/planning watch, not closure.
hazards: Coastal rocks, harbor/quarry edges and wind/wave exposure around Tyludden, Tjuvahålan, Svärjarehålan and Grötvik.
Bathing is user-responsibility; red flag means dangerous bathing on lifeguarded beaches.
